text: That said, it may be beneficial to employ rest intervals of approximately 60 to 90 seconds for single-joint and perhaps certain machine-based exercises because these movements do not show a reduction in volume load from shorter rest, and the heightened metabolic stress may perhaps confer additional anabolic advantages. Evidence suggests that consistently training with shorter rest intervals promotes adaptations that facilitate the ability to sustain a significantly higher mean percentage of 1RM during training (124). These adaptations include increased capillary and mitochondrial density as well as an improved capacity to buffer hydrogen ions and shuttle them out of muscle, thereby minimizing performance decrements.
